simple.meaning: עַצֶּבֶת (ʻatstsebeth) is a Hebrew word meaning “a idol ; also, a pain or wound.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: עַצֶּבֶת (H6094) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Job 9:28, with occurrences in Job, Psalms, Proverbs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עַצֶּבֶת (H6094) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in עַצֶּבֶת (H6094) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: עַצֶּבֶת (ʻatstsebeth) / H6094 is traced through Job 9:28, Psalms 16:4, Psalms 147:3, Proverbs 10:10 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a idol ; also, a pain or wound
definitions.full: H6094. atstsebeth [ עַצֶּ֫בֶת ] noun feminine hurt, injury, pain ; — עַצָּ֑בֶת Prov 10:10 he that winketh with the eye causeth hurt (stirs up strife, etc.); construct עַצְּבַתלֵֿב pain of heart 15:13 (opposed to שָׂמֵחַ לֵב ); plural suffix עַצְּבֹתָ֫י Job 9:28 my pains , so read perhaps also 7:15 (for עַצְמוֺתָ֫י ᵑ0 ); עַצְּבוֺתָם Psa 16:4 (due to idolatry; > idols ᵑ9 ᵑ7 We and others); לְע ׳מְחַבֵּשׁ 147:3 binding up their hurts .

occurrences.englishText: I am afraid of all my sorrows,
Their sorrows shall be multiplied who give gifts to another god.
He heals the broken in heart,
One winking with the eye causes sorrow,
A glad heart makes a cheerful face,
